title: Geometric fibres of profinite tensor schemes over intermediate fields
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $\Omega/k$ a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], let $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(\Omega)$ with its Krull topology, and let $k\subseteq L\subseteq\Omega$ be any intermediate field, including $L=k$ and $L=\Omega$. Use [def-weil-size-convention]. Give $\operatorname{Emb}_k(L,\Omega)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(L,\Omega)$ the topology of restriction to finite intermediate extensions of $k$ in $L$. For a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space $P$, let $LC(P,L)$ be the ring of locally constant functions $P\to L$ with pointwise operations, and write $L[P]$ for the test scheme $(\operatorname{Spec}L)[P]$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor].

There is a canonical identification $L[P]\cong\operatorname{Spec}LC(P,L)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim_i L^{P_i})$, where $P_i$ runs over the finite discrete quotient sets of $P$. The algebra $LC(P,L)$ is ind-etale over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Equip $\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(LC(P,L),\Omega)$ with the topology of restriction to finite etale $k$-subalgebras and with the left action by postcomposition. Evaluation gives a $G$-equivariant homeomorphism
$$\operatorname{Emb}_k(L,\Omega)\times P\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ \operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(LC(P,L),\Omega),\qquad (h,p)\longmapsto(f\longmapsto h(f(p))),$$
where $g\cdot(h,p)=(g\circ h,p)$. For a continuous map $v:P\to Q$, precomposition $LC(Q,L)\to LC(P,L)$ induces $(h,p)\mapsto(h,v(p))$. For an inclusion $L\subseteq M\subseteq\Omega$, the map induced by $LC(P,L)\to LC(P,M)$ is $(h,p)\mapsto(h|_L,p)$. Every $k$-algebra embedding $\Omega\to\Omega$ is an automorphism, and $\operatorname{Emb}_k(\Omega,\Omega)=G$ homeomorphically with the Krull topology. The empty parameter is allowed.

source.place: Examples 4.1.9–4.1.10, pp. 27–28: tensor objects, geometric-point torsor and finite-quotient limits.

proof.text: Take the small directed system of all finite clopen partitions of $P$, with the empty partition when $P=\varnothing$; two partitions have their nonempty intersections as a common refinement. By [lem-sfb-cofinal-clopen-partition-reconstruction], $P=\varprojlim_iP_i$ homeomorphically, where $P_i$ is the finite set of blocks. These are exactly the finite discrete quotient sets up to relabelling. By [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-limit-function-factorization], every locally constant $f:P\to L$ is pulled back from some $P_i$. Pullback $L^{P_i}\to LC(P,L)$ is injective because $P\to P_i$ is surjective; equality of functions from two stages is checked after their common quotient refinement. Consequently these maps exhibit $LC(P,L)=\varinjlim_iL^{P_i}$ as an $L$-algebra: a compatible family of ring maps on the stages extends uniquely by sending a function represented at a stage to its image there. This also works for $P=\varnothing$, whose only quotient is empty and whose function ring is the zero ring.

source.place: Examples 4.1.9–4.1.10, pp. 27–28; explicit finite-stage evaluation calculation

proof.text: For each finite $P_i$, the coordinate idempotents in $L^{P_i}$ give a finite disjoint open covering of its spectrum, with each nonempty chart $D(e_a)=\operatorname{Spec}L$ (localization at $e_a$ is the $a$th factor). Thus $\operatorname{Spec}(L^{P_i})=\coprod_{P_i}\operatorname{Spec}L$, including the empty product. The transition maps are precomposition on coordinates. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-small-colimit-limit] to the small ring diagram of step 1. Its spectrum is precisely the limit defining $L[P]$ in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor], giving both claimed canonical scheme identifications.

source.place: Tag 01YW, lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit; finite product charts as in proetale.tex Tag 097D

proof.text: Every finite family of values in $L$ lies in a finite separable intermediate field $K/k$: the elements are algebraic and separable because $L\subseteq\Omega$, and their compositum is finite separable, as in [def-pd-separable-closure]. Together with step 1, this expresses $LC(P,L)$ as the directed union of the subalgebras $K^{P_i}$, indexed by finite intermediate fields $K\subseteq L$ and finite quotient refinements. Each $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale], and so is the spectrum of $K^{P_i}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-product]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], these are finitely presented etale $k$-algebras. Their filtered union is ind-etale by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. For $P=\varnothing$ the stages are zero, explicitly allowed by the finite-product statement.

source.place: Tag 00U3, lemma-etale-over-field, reverse implication; Tag 00U2, lemma-etale, part (11)

proof.text: Assume first $P\ne\varnothing$. For a $k$-algebra map $\varphi:LC(P,L)\to\Omega$, its kernel is prime. Since a field has just the zero prime, [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-prime-spectrum] gives a unique $p\in P$ with $\ker\varphi=\{f:f(p)=0\}$. Restriction to constant functions defines a unital $k$-algebra map $h:L\to\Omega$, which is injective since $L$ is a field. For every $f$, the function $f-\operatorname{const}(f(p))$ belongs to this kernel, so $\varphi(f)=h(f(p))$. Conversely this formula defines a $k$-algebra map for every $(h,p)$. Its restriction to constants recovers $h$, and its kernel recovers $p$, proving bijectivity. If $P=\varnothing$, no unital map from the zero ring to the field $\Omega$ exists, so both sides are empty.

source.place: Examples 4.1.9–4.1.10, pp. 27–28; explicit finite-stage evaluation calculation

proof.text: Let $B=LC(P,L)$. The stages $K^{P_i}$ of step 3 are cofinal among finite etale $k$-subalgebras of $B$: by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product], such a subalgebra $A$ is finite-dimensional over $k$; finitely many basis functions are contained in a common stage, hence so is $A$. On $K^{P_i}$, the evaluation formula depends only on the pair $(h|_K,\pi_i(p))$, which takes values in the product of two discrete sets. Both coordinate maps are continuous by the restriction topology on embeddings and the quotient topology on $P_i$. The induced map to the discrete set $\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(K^{P_i},\Omega)$ is therefore continuous. Restricting further to $A$ proves continuity for every finite etale restriction, hence continuity of the evaluation bijection.

source.place: Examples 4.1.9–4.1.10, pp. 27–28; explicit finite-stage evaluation calculation

proof.text: The inverse is continuous as follows. Its embedding coordinate $\varphi\mapsto h$ is continuous on restriction to every finite $K\subseteq L$, since the constant functions $K$ form a finite etale subalgebra by step 3 (when $P\ne\varnothing$). Its point coordinate is also continuous: the map $\varphi\mapsto\ker\varphi\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ has inverse image of a basic open $D(f)$ equal to $\{\varphi:\varphi(f)\ne0\}$. By step 3, $f$ lies in a finite etale stage, so this set is open in the restriction topology. Compose this continuous kernel map with the inverse of the homeomorphism in [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-prime-spectrum] and project to $P$. These are exactly the two coordinates of the inverse in step 4. For empty $P$ the map between empty spaces is a homeomorphism.

source.place: Examples 4.1.9–4.1.10, pp. 27–28; explicit finite-stage evaluation calculation

proof.text: Postcomposition by $g\in G$ takes $\varphi(f)=h(f(p))$ to $g(h(f(p)))$, hence acts as $(h,p)\mapsto(g\circ h,p)$. For continuous $v:P\to Q$ and $f\in LC(Q,L)$, evaluating precomposition gives $h((f\circ v)(p))=h(f(v(p)))$, so the map is $(h,p)\mapsto(h,v(p))$. For $L\subseteq M$ and $h:M\to\Omega$, restriction of the same formula to $LC(P,L)$ is $(h|_L,p)$. These identities prove all equivariance and naturality assertions directly, including composites and empty sources.

source.place: Examples 4.1.9–4.1.10, pp. 27–28; explicit finite-stage evaluation calculation

proof.text: Finally, let $a:\Omega\to\Omega$ be a $k$-algebra embedding and $x\in\Omega$. Algebraicity from [def-pd-separable-closure] supplies a nonzero $F\in k[T]$ with $F(x)=0$. The finite set $R=\{y\in\Omega:F(y)=0\}$ is mapped into itself by $a$ and $a$ is injective, so its restriction is a permutation of $R$. Thus $x=a(y)$ for some $y\in R$. As $x$ was arbitrary, $a$ is surjective and therefore an automorphism. The resulting identity of embedding and automorphism sets identifies the topologies: a basic neighbourhood of $g$ on either side consists of those maps agreeing with $g$ on a finite intermediate field $K$, equivalently the coset $g\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$. This is precisely the Krull neighbourhood basis, so the identity is a homeomorphism.
